why: A protocol's numbers decide what counts as passing, and nothing used to notice them moving: the criteria table's digests cover kinds and cases, the suite lock covers the ground, and the migration proof compares one record's verdicts rather than the declared numbers -- so a threshold edit left the whole offline suite green (acceptance/records/2026-09-23-threshold-pilot.md).

This table pins the bytes of the protocols in use, so a moved number fails the gate until this table says the new bytes are the ones meant. The reason field is part of the entry because a digest can show that something moved and cannot show that anyone looked.

Editing this table is the approval act, and it is a human one: pasting the digest the gate prints is bookkeeping, not review. Clearing the gate afterwards says the file and the table agree -- never that the change was approved.

Which protocols this table has to cover is read off protocols/ rather than declared here, because a list only holds what somebody remembered to add: the day after this table landed, 6de88a0 added lizard2_flat_v2.json and nothing said a word. The one exemption is a rule, not a second list -- the name+version pairs in baseline_metrics.LEGACY_PROTOCOLS are the protocols published before there was an anchor to carry.

protocols/baseline_flat_v4.json.reason: Frozen at the criteria-identity change: v4 renames the criteria and changes no number. A threshold edit belongs in a new protocol file, because old records carry this file's digest.

protocols/lizard2_flat_v1.json.reason: Frozen when the lizard2 line's protocol landed (banded criteria, judge baseline-criteria-banded-1). Its suite_expected pins the ground; the thresholds it reads were unguarded until this table.

protocols/lizard2_flat_v2.json.reason: Frozen with the two banded-criteria fixes and the settled reader (6de88a0). v1 stays anchored too: it keeps answering the records that name it.

protocols/locomotion_eval_v4.yaml.reason: The locomotion path's current protocol. Its suite_expected pins the ground a run was measured on; this pins the numbers it was judged by -- the same value the eval records already carry as eval_protocol.digest.

protocols/locomotion_eval_v3.yaml.reason: Superseded by v4, kept so the records that name it stay readable.

protocols/locomotion_eval_v2.yaml.reason: Superseded by v4, kept so the records that name it stay readable.
